posts.title: The Download: preserving minds and weighing open AI risks
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind As we age, we forget most of what we’ve experienced, yet there’s still undeniable continuity: At 30, or 50, or 70, you will still…
bullets: The debate over open-source frontier AI models has intensified following Anthropic's warning that a Z.ai model poses significant cyberattack risks due to its unrestricted accessibility.
A major geopolitical and corporate security scandal has emerged involving the alleged illicit acquisition of $7.5 billion worth of restricted Nvidia chips.
COP31's flagship initiative to electrify 35% of energy use is failing to gain traction, with only about a dozen nations currently prepared to sign the pledge.
The electrification goal is particularly challenging as it requires a fourfold increase in the current global pace of energy transition.

posts.title: Intel Earnings, AMD Earnings, Intel and AMD’s Divergence
posts.summary: Intel and AMD's diverging earnings point to fundamental historical differences, and make me wonder if Intel needs to find a new (old) path.
bullets: Intel and AMD are exhibiting a stark divergence in financial performance, highlighting fundamental differences in their historical business models and strategic execution.
The disparity in earnings suggests that Intel's current operational trajectory may be unsustainable, necessitating a potential pivot back to its core historical strengths.

The market performance of these two semiconductor giants serves as a case study in how legacy architectural advantages and manufacturing strategies impact long-term viability in the modern tech landscape.

posts.title: Blog Review: Nov. 11
posts.summary:
Interconnects key in AI infrastructure; floating nets; mitigating Control Flow attacks; PNT trends; SEMI Market Symposium.
The post Blog Review: Nov. 11 appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Industry experts project that AI infrastructure growth will drive the semiconductor industry toward a $3 trillion revenue milestone over the next decade.
Interconnect technology is identified as the primary bottleneck for AI compute scaling, requiring exponential speed increases to keep pace with processor performance.
New security and reliability concerns are emerging, including hidden floating nets in analog circuits and control flow attacks that threaten system-level integrity.
Market trends indicate a shift toward resilient position, navigation, and timing (PNT) technologies and advanced packaging lithography to reduce yield-related trial and error.

posts.title: China NEV sales rise 13.1% to record 1.94 million in October, CAAM data shows
posts.summary:
BEVs continued to lead growth, with October sales reaching a record 1.353 million units, up 22% year-on-year.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's NEV sales hit a record 1.94 million units in October, up 13.1% year-on-year, with NEVs capturing 64.3% of the total vehicle market.
Exports have become a critical growth engine, surging 140% year-on-year to 606,000 units and accounting for over 31% of total NEV sales.
While BEV sales grew 22% year-on-year, domestic NEV sales actually declined by 8.6%, highlighting that international demand is currently offsetting domestic market saturation.

posts.title: VW Anhui reportedly has no new models planned for 2027-2028 as ID. UNYX sales disappoint
posts.summary:
Volkswagen Anhui had considered launching a crossover in 2028, but that project has also been put on hold.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Volkswagen Anhui has halted plans for new vehicle launches in 2027 and 2028, including a previously considered crossover, due to poor performance of the ID. UNYX series.
The ID. UNYX series has significantly underperformed, recording only 11,360 sales in the first nine months of 2026 against an internal 2027 target of 128,000 units.
Volkswagen China maintains that it will still introduce 30 new energy vehicle models through 2029, though it declined to clarify if any of these will be all-new models from the Anhui joint venture.
